definition: Software capable of tasks that used to require a human brain (understanding, deciding, creating). "Classical AI" is specialized; generative AI is versatile.

definition: An AI that produces new content (text, image, code) from a simple instruction, instead of executing a single programmed task.

definition: The engine behind assistants like Claude or ChatGPT: a model trained on enormous amounts of text that predicts the most plausible continuation of what you type.

definition: The basic unit an LLM reads and produces: a chunk of a word. The length of exchanges and their cost are measured in tokens.

definition: When an LLM confidently invents a false answer. Hence the basic rule: verify facts, numbers, and references.

definition: The instruction you give the AI. A good prompt — clear, with the context and the goal — changes the result of one answer. But what weighs on every answer is the context (CLAUDE.md, Brain, skills).
Capable of processing multiple types of input — text, image, audio — not just text.

definition: A model you can download and self-host (e.g. Llama, Mistral), as opposed to "closed" models accessible only via a service.

definition: The American lab that creates Claude, focused on model reliability and safety.

Anthropic's AI assistant. A family of models (in 2026: Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku — the Claude 5 family) and several products: Chat (to talk things through), Cowork (to delegate office work), Code (to act inside a project).
Claude's four sizes: Fable (the class above, the most capable), Opus (the heavyweight), Sonnet (the balanced one), Haiku (the fast one). Rule: the cheapest one that gets the job done.

Three ways to use Claude: talk things through (Chat), delegate office work with no terminal (Cowork — desktop, web, mobile), act on files and projects (Code — terminal, browser, mobile). House rule: Chat writes, Code executes.
The window where you type commands instead of clicking. Looks scary, but it runs on copy-paste.
A programmed pipe connecting two pieces of software. It's one of the ways to connect a service to Claude, in an automated way.

An open standard created by Anthropic in late 2024: a "universal plug" to connect Claude to tools (Shopify, Drive, Gmail, GitHub…) with no custom integration. In the Claude apps, it's called a connector. Since 2026, Claude doesn't just read anymore: it acts, subject to validation.

Claude given a goal and the means to act on its own, in a loop, until it delivers — instead of just answering. In 2026: inside a session, as subagents, as scheduled routines, or hosted on a server. Always within a frame: goal, budget, frequency, success criterion.
An online space where your project lives with its full history; once connected, updates deploy themselves.
The "folder" of a project on GitHub, with all its files and history.
A saved, timestamped version of a project on GitHub. You can always go back to it.

A timer that runs a task automatically at regular intervals (e.g. every morning at 7 a.m.). The "infrastructure" form of recurring tasks, alongside loops (ephemeral) and routines (scheduled on Claude's side).
A standard format for automatically pulling new articles from a site. The basic building block of any news watch.
A program that posts messages on Telegram; a public channel is followable by anyone via a simple link.

A file Claude reads at startup: tone, conventions, pitfalls turned into rules. It saves you from re-explaining everything in every conversation. Versioned in the repo (CLAUDE-{domain}-{project}.md convention), short, reviewed on a set schedule. Facts go in the Brain, procedures go in skills.

A method (popularized by Kieran Klaassen and Dan Shipper, at Every) where every lesson becomes a reusable rule: your system gets better with use. In Hugo's setup, two levels: one mistake → one CLAUDE.md rule; one session → one capture in the Brain.

Programming by describing what you want in plain language and letting the AI generate the code. A term popularized by Andrej Karpathy in 2025. Commonplace by 2026: what sets you apart now is context engineering.
The art of ranking well in search engines (Google…).
SEO's equivalent for AI: optimizing your content to get **cited** by assistants (ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity). That's the goal of this site.

The durable memory of what we know and decide: a private repo of Markdown files (entities, building blocks, projects, method, notes, sessions) that every AI reads through a connector. Rule: a stale brain is worse than an empty brain.

An open specification published by Google Cloud in June 2026: Markdown files with a YAML header (a single required field, "type"), connected by links, with an index. It formalizes Karpathy's "LLM wiki". The Brain's format.
The few "key: value" lines at the top of a Markdown file (type, title, description, tags, date…). It's what makes a plain text file machine-readable — the basis of OKF.

Everything the model "sees" at the moment it answers: the instruction, context files, documents, history, tool results — nothing else. Limited (up to one million tokens on Claude 5) and re-read with every answer. Context engineering is organizing what the AI knows.

When a conversation gets too long, the tool replaces its beginning with an automatic summary. Useful, but the summary keeps what the model considers essential — hence the handoff brief and the capture in the Brain.

The validated summary you ask Claude for when a conversation runs long — where things stand, what's decided, what's left, the constraints — so you can start a fresh conversation without losing anything.

The feature that lets Claude remember your preferences and your projects' context from one conversation to the next (shared between chat and Cowork since August 2026). Implicit and tied to one tool, unlike the Brain — the memory you choose, can re-read, and share.
A procedure packaged in a folder (a SKILL.md file, sometimes scripts) that Claude loads on demand when your request matches. Written know-how, portable from one tool to the next.

projets.label: The site redesign, published with a skill

definition: A script that fires automatically at a specific point in Claude's work (before a command, after an edit). Deterministic: it checks, blocks, or logs, without thinking. A rule gets read; a hook gets run.

A Claude the main agent hands a subtask to, with its own context, in the background. To parallelize, isolate a heavy read, or specialize (reviewer, verifier). A workflow orchestrates several subagents.
A versioned package bundling skills, subagents, commands, hooks, and connectors, installable in one command — from a marketplace, or to share know-how with a team.
A tool plugged into Claude (Shopify, Gmail, Drive, GitHub…) from a menu in the Claude apps. Under the hood, an MCP. Rule: the assistant never has more rights than the person talking to it.
A prompt re-run at regular intervals by an agent, inside your Claude Code session, to watch or check something for a few hours. Ephemeral: it expires on its own.

A scheduled agent (every morning, every Monday) that runs in the cloud on Claude's side — Claude Code on the web, Cowork, or a hosted agent — without your machine. The link between the ephemeral loop and your own infrastructure (cron).

A small script that orchestrates several subagents deterministically — a review per dimension, then a check of every finding, for example. Available in Claude Code since June 2026. Save it for tasks that deserve a dozen agents.
Claude's agent that acts inside a project: reads and edits files, runs commands, deploys. In the terminal, the browser, the desktop app, or on mobile (cloud session). Included in every paid plan.

Claude's assistant for office work, which carries out a job end to end with no terminal: files, spreadsheets, presentations, a built-in browser, routines, and learning a skill by recording your screen. On desktop, web, and mobile since summer 2026.
In Claude Code, the mode where Claude decides routine permissions on its own, with protections against manipulation. Became the default in August 2026.

Booby-trapped instructions hidden in a web page or an email an agent reads, to push it into doing something other than its task. 2026 models resist it far better; the real protection is still limited rights.

The principle: the AI reads, analyzes, and proposes automatically; a person validates anything that changes a price, a stock level, a campaign, an email, or a publication. The flow: request → analysis → preview → validation → execution → log → measurement.
Said of an action you can run several times without producing several effects. It's what makes an automation recoverable: replaying a publication or an import duplicates nothing.

The system I'm building to run my companies with AI: a shared foundation (database, AI layer, identity and rights, action log) and five building blocks — Zéro, Knowledge, Content Machine, Growth, Socle IA (AI Core). One core, several contexts.

projets.label: HL OS: five building blocks, one foundation

definition: In HL OS, a system under construction: a scope, a living specification, a development plan with success criteria ("we'll know it's right when…"), and a dated Decisions section.

HL OS's "action-first" decision building block: it brings together sales, acquisition, SEO, web, email, and social, and proposes a handful of actions ranked by impact, confidence, effort, and risk, with their evidence. Automatic reads, validated writes. In production for Cobra since September 2026.

projets.label: Growth: replacing ten dashboards with an action queue

definition: HL OS's publishing building block: one capture, N destinations. The base unit is the attested observation; a post or an article is just a rendering of it, proposed by the machine and validated by a human. Never a publication without validation.

A few media files, a voice memo, or a note, at a place, at a time, by an identified person. The Content Machine's base unit. "Witnessed" (seen in the field) and "documented" (read, owned) are kept separate, both in the database and in the rendering.

Who, where, when behind a piece of content. The first-hand experience signal that search engines and answering AIs reward — and the exact opposite of mass-generated content. "Provenance is the product."

Turning existing material (a magazine article, an archive) into renderings suited to other destinations (social, website, newsletter). In the Content Machine, the "documented" material from Haute Fidélité magazine.
A date before which a piece of content can't go out. In the Content Machine, it's a lock, not an instruction: the door stays shut until the date.
The HL OS building block that sorts and summarizes emails and turns an email into a task. The Brain's daily signal source, and one of the publishing triggers ("to publish").

HL OS's shared AI layer: writing in my voice, embeddings for search, a router that picks the model by tier and logs every call, and a server-side encrypted-secrets pattern. The other building blocks call it; they don't reimplement it.

Haute Fidélité's in-house ERP, built from scratch in five days with Claude Code in June 2026 (CRM, ad sales, invoicing, payment reminders). Now the technical foundation of HL OS: a single application (headless CMS + web framework + PostgreSQL).

guides.label: Do you still need to buy an ERP

definition: A company's central management software (sales, purchasing, inventory, invoicing). At Cobra: Odoo, extended almost daily with Claude Code. At Haute Fidélité: HF-OS, custom-built.

guides.label: Do you still need to buy an ERP

definition: The open-source ERP Cobra runs on (sales, purchasing, inventory, invoicing), extended with in-house modules. The commercial truth: actual sales, margin, stock.

The e-commerce platform behind the Cobra and Haute Fidélité stores. It describes the web flow; Odoo carries the actuals. Plugged into Claude through a connector, and open to shopping agents since 2026.

The document that describes what we want to build: where, what, what must not change. At Cobra, every Odoo change has its numbered CDC — and since 2026, the AI re-reads the request and checks its assumptions against the real database before a single line is written.

projets.label: AI verifies what it assumes before coding

definition: Build it yourself or buy it (or have it built). In 2026, AI is collapsing the cost of customization: the math flips for anything specific to a business — from the ERP to the steering layer.

guides.label: Do you still need to buy an ERP

definition: A merge request: a batch of changes proposed on GitHub, reviewed and automatically checked (CI) before it enters the production version. Claude Code's unit of work. HF-OS: 96 PRs in five days.

The automatic checks that run on every change to a project (lint, tests, build) or on a schedule (GitHub Actions). In my case: auto-translating pages, regenerating the indexes, a weekly consistency check.
Pushing to production the exact commit of one feature, never a whole branch where developments are mixed together. A hard rule born from a production release that broke everything in May 2026.
A signal one service sends automatically to another when something happens (an order placed, a status changed). The opposite of a cron: you don't go check, you get notified.

Turning a text into a sequence of numbers that captures its meaning, to find documents that are close in meaning rather than in wording. The basis of a semantic search index — the one the Brain doesn't need yet.

Having the model look up the relevant documents (via embeddings) before answering, instead of relying on its memory. The Brain does the same thing by navigation, with no index — for as long as that's enough.

A database that stores embeddings and finds the ones closest to a question. In HL OS: PostgreSQL with the pgvector extension, planned as an index derived from the Brain — rebuilt from the files, never the source of truth.
The open-source database that serves as the foundation for HF-OS and the HL OS building blocks. One single database, shared.
A content management system that provides an admin and an API without dictating how things are displayed. HF-OS runs on a headless CMS (Payload) and a web framework (Next.js) in a single application.

guides.label: Do you still need to buy an ERP

definition: Producing the page as complete HTML on the server, rather than building it in the browser with JavaScript. Essential to be read by AI crawlers, which don't run JavaScript.

projets.label: The AI Watch made visible to LLMs

definition: A machine-readable block of data, placed in a page, that says who's speaking and about what (author, article, question/answer). The vocabulary is schema.org. On every page of this site.
A text file at the root of a site that summarizes its content for AIs, page by page (plus its extended version, llms-full.txt, with the full text). An agent's entry point to this site.

My two Claudes, deliberately kept apart: HL (personal account — steering, strategy, editorial, method, this site) and Cobra (company account — Odoo and Shopify dev, purely technical). The badges on every journal entry.
The end-of-session ritual: re-read, write the session entry in the Brain, propose updates to the reference pages touched, run the confidentiality filter. The second level of Compound Engineering.
In the Brain, a page whose title is real but whose content doesn't exist yet: it says so and asks questions instead of answering them. You never make up the content of a shell.

The class of Claude models above Opus, inaugurated by Fable 5 in June 2026. "Mythos" also refers to the version without certain guardrails, reserved for trusted-access programs (Project Glasswing: cyberdefense, life sciences).

The model reusing what it has already read in a conversation, billed at a fraction of the price. A well-structured conversation (stable context first, variable questions after) costs less than a messy one.
The sub-channels of a Telegram group. In the Content Machine, one topic per context (personal, work, magazine): posting in the right topic says where the capture comes from, with no manual tag.
